newsitem.title: UK: Britain sells stakes in utilities for 257 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: Britain sells stakes in utilities for 257 mln stg.

text.p: The British government sold residual stakeholdings in several utilities for a total 257 million pounds ($428.7 million) through a competitive auction organised by bankers Rothschild, acting for the Treasury, a statement said on Tuesday.
It said that 81 million shares in British Energy Plc had been sold to HSBC James Capel, which analysts said was equivalent to just over 12 percent of the company.

The sale also included 18.8 million shares in Scottish Power Plc which analysts said amounted to around 1.6 percent of the comany, to Dresdner Kleinwort Benson and the two stocks showed highest volumes on the market on Tuesday.
The treasury also sold small residual stakes in National Grid, Northern Ireland Electricity, Scottish Hydro-Electric, National Power, PowerGen, Severn Trent, South West Water and Wessex Water.

The flotation of British Energy in July at a first instalment price of 100 pence for the retail offer and 105 pence for institutions flopped as the shares opened at 98 pence and the government was left with a 12.27 percent stake.

But British Energy turned in strong first half results last week with losses narrowing to 53 million pounds from 169 million pounds a year ago helped to confirm a rising trend in the share price which brought them to 147.5 pence by 1148 GMT. ($1=.5995 Pound)
